title: 💳 You buy a shirt on installments and they ask about your house rent! New European rules change buy-now-pay-later
body: 💳 You buy a shirt on installments and they ask about your house rent! New European rules change buy-now-pay-later

New European rules began applying in Germany on November 20, and they could make buy-now-pay-later stores such as Klarna and PayPal ask you about your income and expenses — and perhaps the value of your house rent — before agreeing to split your purchases into installments.

The rule is the revised version of the European consumer credit directive, which now covers small short-term interest-free loans — exactly the territory of 'buy now, pay later' offers — after these offers mostly escaped strict credit rules, with the goal that fewer people fall into debt.

Providers must now assess the customer's ability to pay based on information about income, expenses and other financial obligations, not only on a record of late payments — which could mean being asked what remains of your salary after fixed expenses, and users on social media have already reported questions of this kind from well-known payment providers.

Before these rules, thorough checks applied only from 200 euros, and the option to pay after 30 or 45 days was mostly exempt; now the rules cover even small amounts and short terms, while payment deferral offered by the store itself without a financing company remains a different case, and can last up to 50 days.

But the law itself does not specifically require asking about rent, nor does it specify what data must be collected or how often — it only requires the information to be proportionate to the amount, duration and risk, and to follow the data-minimization principle in privacy laws, so only what is necessary and appropriate may be collected.

One helpful change for consumers is that if an automated check rejects you at payment, you have the right to ask for an understandable explanation of why you were rejected — although this does not give you a right to the credit — and your credit record may also be checked, so it is worth thinking twice before using buy-now-pay-later for small purchases.
Simply put: a shirt on installments could cost you disclosing your rent and income... would you agree to share your financial data in exchange for delaying payment?
Do you use 'buy now, pay later' services or pay immediately to avoid the questions?
